Complete Empirical Research Plan ― “Weather, Mortality, and Adaptation in U.S. Counties, 1950-2020”

=======================================================================

1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------
Method: Difference-in-Differences (continuous treatment, high-dimensional fixed-effects) combined with an event-study specification to trace adaptation.

Why appropriate  
• Daily weather shocks are plausibly as-good-as-random after conditioning on county and time fixed effects.  
• DID with county × year FE (or county + year FE plus long-run climate controls) isolates within-county, across-year deviations (“weather anomalies”) from permanent climatic differences.  
• Event-study interactions of anomalies with decade (or with the year relative to the local arrival of residential air-conditioning) let us observe how the weather–mortality gradient evolves, i.e. adaptation.

Formula (baseline)

MortRate_{c,t} = β₁ HeatAnom_{c,t} + β₂ ColdAnom_{c,t}  
                   + Σ_d β_d (HeatAnom_{c,t} × Decade_d)             (Adaptation)  
                   + δ_c  + γ_t  + X_{c,t}′θ + ε_{c,t}

where  
• HeatAnom = (∑ degree-days above 27 °C in county-year) – county-specific long-run mean.  
• ColdAnom analogous (< 10 °C).  
• δ_c = county fixed effects, γ_t = year fixed effects (absorb national trends, medical progress, etc.).  
• X_{c,t} = time-varying county covariates (income, age-structure, population).  
Identification uses the interaction of high-frequency randomness in weather with time to generate a “treated” vs. “control” contrast.

2. Treatment and Control
------------------------
Treatment variable  
• Continuous: HeatAnom_{c,t} (or number of “extreme-heat days” > 90 °F). We will standardise (mean 0, SD 1) for interpretability.

Control group  
• Observations in the same county in years with lower (or negative) heat anomalies provide the counterfactual. Because weather varies year-to-year, every county serves at different times as treated or control.

Treatment timing  
• Not discrete; realised each calendar year.  
• For adaptation, we treat “decade” as event time. Alternatively, we can define t = 0 as the first census year in which county AC penetration > 50 %, and estimate an event-study around that adoption year.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------
A1. Exogeneity of short-run weather shocks  
 Plausibility: Very high; county-level daily temperature is determined by atmospheric physics, not mortality.

A2. Parallel trends / common shocks conditional on FE  
 Plausibility: Reasonable—after removing county & year FE, no reason to expect systematic correlation between residual mortality trends and weather anomalies. Still testable via placebo leads.

A3. No simultaneous shocks that are *caused* by weather and independently affect mortality (omitted variables)  
 Ex: power outages, wildfires; we control for precipitation anomalies and county×year socio-economic controls. Residual risk remains.

A4. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA)  
 Individual mortality reacts to local weather, spillovers across counties minimal because counties are spatially small vs. atmospheric systems.

A5. Composition stability  
 Migration induced by weather is slow relative to annual frequency; including county-year population controls mitigates.

4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
-----------------------------------------
T1. Long-run climatic trends (global warming) confounded with medical progress  
 Fix: Include year FE (absorbs national secular mortality decline); use anomalies (de-trend weather).  

T2. Measurement error in mortality (small counties)  
 Fix: Weight regressions by county population; aggregate to age-specific mortality to increase counts; cluster SE at county.  

T3. Endogenous local adaptation investments (e.g. counties that face frequent heat waves buy more AC which directly reduces mortality)  
 Threat because adaptation is itself *induced* by past weather.  
 Fix: Treat adaptation as outcome, not confounder. In baseline we estimate short-run effect; in separate event-study we explicitly model AC penetration. For contemporaneous bias, we show robustness to controlling for county-specific linear trend interacted with local climate normals.

5. R Code Outline
-----------------
```r
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# ------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast high-dimensional FE
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Assume three CSVs: daily weather, mortality, covariates
weather_daily <- fread("weather_daily.csv")   # date, fips, tmax, tmin
mort_daily    <- fread("mortality_daily.csv") # date, fips, deaths
cov_county    <- fread("county_covariates.csv") # year, fips, pop, income, ac_share

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Construct county-year panel
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2a: Degree-days by county-year
weather_daily[, 
    `:=`(heat_dd = pmax((tmax + tmin)/2 - 27, 0),    # °C basis
         cold_dd = pmax(10 - (tmax + tmin)/2, 0))
]

dd_year <- weather_daily[, .(
    heat_dd = sum(heat_dd),          # total degree-days above threshold
    cold_dd = sum(cold_dd)
), by = .(fips, year = year(date))]

# STEP 2b: Mortality counts per county-year
mort_year <- mort_daily[, .(
    deaths = sum(deaths)
), by = .(fips, year = year(date))]

# STEP 2c: Merge & create mortality rate
panel <- merge(dd_year, mort_year, by = c("fips", "year"))
panel <- merge(panel, cov_county, by = c("fips", "year"))

panel[, mort_rate := deaths / pop * 1e5]  # deaths per 100,000

# Calculate long-run county averages (1950-1980 baseline)
climate_norm <- panel[year %between% c(1950, 1980),
                      .(heat_norm = mean(heat_dd), cold_norm = mean(cold_dd)),
                      by = fips]
panel <- merge(panel, climate_norm, by = "fips", all.x = TRUE)

# Weather anomalies
panel[, `:=`(
      heat_anom = (heat_dd - heat_norm)/sd(heat_dd), 
      cold_anom = (cold_dd - cold_norm)/sd(cold_dd)
)]

# Decade dummies
panel[, decade := floor(year/10)*10]
for(d in seq(1960, 2020, 10)){
  panel[, paste0("D", d) := (decade == d)]
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main regression
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# High-dimensional FE: county & year
reg_main <- feols(mort_rate ~ heat_anom + cold_anom | fips + year, 
                  weights = ~pop, cluster = ~fips, data = panel)
summary(reg_main)

# Adaptation: interaction with decade
reg_adapt <- feols(
  mort_rate ~ heat_anom*factor(decade) + cold_anom | fips + year,
  weights = ~pop, cluster = ~fips, data = panel)
summary(reg_adapt)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Robustness Check: Placebo leads
# ------------------------------------------------------------
panel[, lead_heat := shift(heat_anom, +1L, type = "lag"), by = fips]
reg_placebo <- feols(mort_rate ~ lead_heat + heat_anom + cold_anom | fips + year,
                     weights = ~pop, cluster = ~fips, data = panel)
summary(reg_placebo)
```

6. Expected Results
-------------------
Economic and medical literature find “heat kills”. Prior:  
• β₁ < 0 for cold anomalies (cold raises mortality), β₁ > 0 for heat anomalies (heat raises mortality).  
• Magnitude: One SD increase in annual extreme-heat degree-days raises all-age mortality by roughly 0.5–1.0 deaths per 100,000 (≈0.3 % of mean).  
Adaptation: Interaction terms should show a declining (less positive) heat coefficient over decades, especially after 1980 (diffusion of air-conditioning).

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
-------------------------------------------
C1: Exogeneity of treatment  … 1  
C2: Parallel trends conditional on FE … 0.8 (credible but testable)  
C3: No spillovers/SUTVA … 0.9  
C4: No differential measurement/attrition … 0.8  
C5: Correct functional form & no anticipation … 0.7  

(Overall ≈ 4.2/5; some residual concern on differential adaptation bias and functional-form misspecification.)

=======================================================================
